text:
The water is gone. In its place lies a vast, rectangular scar of polished concrete, cold as a tombstone in the January wind. Twenty years have stripped the paint from the lane markers, leaving faint, ghostly blue lines that fade into the gray slush gathering at the deep end. The starting blocks stand like silent sentinels, their rubber grips cracked and peeling, waiting for feet that will never again press down with the force of human ambition.

Here, the air tastes of rust and old chlorine, a phantom scent clinging to the porous walls. No splashing echoes off the tiled ceiling; no crowd roars in the stands above. Only the brittle snap of ice forming on the gutter drains breaks the silence. This is not a monument to victory, but a hollow shell where triumph evaporated, leaving only the stark geometry of absence against the winter sky.
